turns.response_html:
That is a Bernzomatic ST2200 Micro Torch. It’s a handy tool for detail work like soldering, heat shrinking, or even some kitchen tasks.

Here is the quick breakdown on how to get it running safely:

1. Refilling (If it's empty)

Since these ship empty for safety, you’ll likely need to fill it with butane (the same stuff used for lighters).

  • Turn the torch upside down.
  • Press the butane canister tip into the fill valve on the bottom of the torch for about 5–10 seconds.
  • Wait a few minutes before lighting it to let any escaped gas dissipate and the liquid butane reach room temperature.

2. Adjusting the Flame

  • On the side or top, there is usually a small airflow control lever (it looks like a metal tab). This adjusts the flame from a "torch" (blue, pinpoint) to a "lighter" (yellow, soft) flame.
  • There is also a flame adjustment knob (often near the base or on the side) to control the height/intensity.

3. Lighting It

  1. Safety Lock: Most models have a safety trigger. You may need to press a button or slide a latch before the ignition trigger will move.
  2. Ignite: Press the large ignition button on the back with your thumb. You should hear a click and see the flame start.
  3. Continuous Use: If you want it to stay on without holding the button, look for the "Continuous" slide switch (labeled on the side of your torch). Slide it over while the flame is active to lock it on.

4. Turning It Off

  • If you are holding the trigger, just let go.
  • If you used the continuous lock, slide that switch back to the "off" position.

⚠️ A Quick Safety Note: The metal nozzle stays extremely hot for several minutes after the flame is out. Don't toss it back into a tool bag or drawer until it has completely cooled down.

turns.prompt_text: I have some butane here with me but I'm just can't tell if it's being filled or not
turns.response_html:
When you press the butane canister down, you should feel the torch get noticeably colder and hear a slight hissing sound as the liquid transfers.

If the butane is just spraying out of the sides, try these three things:

  • Use an adapter: Most butane caps come with a set of plastic tips; find the one that fits your torch's valve snugly.
  • Purge the air: Use a small screwdriver to briefly press the refill valve (without the butane can) to let out any trapped air pressure.
  • Vertical pressure: Ensure you are pressing straight down with the torch and the can completely upside down.

You’ll know it’s full when the butane starts to sputter or spray back at you.

To help you fill your Bernzomatic ST2200, here are the most helpful videos specifically showing the refill process for Bernzomatic micro torches.

Key Video Guides

  • Official Bernzomatic Guide (Refill Focus): How to Refill a Butane Torch
    • What to look for: This video shows the "sputtering" effect you should see when the tank is completely full.
  • Quick Demonstration: How to Use the Bernzomatic Detail Torch
    • What to look for: A clear visual of the fill port on the bottom of the tool and how to align the canister.

Troubleshooting the "Am I actually filling it?" feeling

If you aren't sure if fuel is going in, here is what the experts in these videos suggest:

  1. Check for Temperature Change: As the liquid butane enters the torch, the handle will become significantly colder to the touch. This is the most reliable sign that the transfer is happening.
  2. The "Sputter" Test: Continue holding the can down firmly. Once the torch is full, liquid butane will start to spray out or "sputter" from the valve. That is your signal to stop.
  3. Purge the Air (The "Burp"): If the torch feels light and won't take fuel, it might have an air pocket. Use a small screwdriver or a paperclip to briefly press the refill valve on the torch (without the butane can) to let out any trapped air. You’ll hear a quick hiss. After that, try filling again.
  4. Wait Before Lighting: After you think it's full, let the torch sit for 3 to 5 minutes. This allows the liquid fuel to stabilize and reach room temperature, which prevents large "flare-ups" when you first ignite it.

Since you've been working with 3D printers and electronics lately, this torch is great for heat-shrinking tubing on your wiring projects once you get it fueled up!

If you don't hear a hiss, the gas flow is likely blocked or turned off.

  • Turn the adjustment dial: Look for the knob (usually on the bottom or side) and rotate it toward the plus (+) sign. If it’s dialed all the way to minus, no gas will exit the nozzle.
  • Check the "Continuous" lock: Ensure the slide switch is in the off position before you pull the trigger; sometimes the ignition won't engage if the lock was already slid over.
  • Listen closely: Press the trigger halfway down—you should hear a distinct shhh sound of escaping gas.

Do you hear that hissing sound now when you turn the dial to the max setting?

If the knob is at max and you still hear nothing, the nozzle is likely clogged or there is an airlock in the tank.

Try purging the air by using a small tool to press the refill valve on the bottom (away from your face) until the hissing stops, then refill it for just 3 seconds. If that fails, tap the side of the torch firmly against your palm to dislodge any debris in the internal gas line.

Do you see a small blue spark inside the nozzle when you pull the trigger?

Since there is a spark but no hiss, gas isn't reaching the nozzle. Try turning the dial back and forth a few times to clear any internal debris, then leave it at the mid-point and try again.

If that fails, purge the tank by pressing the bottom refill valve with a pen to release trapped air, then refill it briefly.

turns.prompt_text: I really think that I'm just not loading the butane correctly
turns.response_html:
It's very common for the nozzle and valve to not seal perfectly during the fill. Try these quick fixes:

  • Check the nozzle: Many butane cans have a universal tip, but your torch might need one of the plastic adapters usually found in the can's cap.
  • Press harder: You often have to use a surprising amount of firm, vertical force to open the internal valve and let the liquid flow.
  • The "Hiss" Test: After "filling," press the refill valve on the torch with a pen; if no gas sprays out, the tank is definitely empty.

Would you like me to find a photo of the specific adapter tip usually needed for Bernzomatic valves?

Many butane canisters come with a set of plastic adapters like these tucked into the underside of the cap. For the Bernzomatic ST2200, you are looking for a tip that fits snugly over the brass valve on the bottom of the torch without wobbling.

If you don't have these, or if the metal stem of the butane can doesn't seem to reach the valve, that is likely why it isn't filling.

Try this "Check" to be sure: 1. Take a small screwdriver or a pen. 2. Quickly press the brass pin on the bottom of the torch for just a split second. 3. If you hear a loud "psst" and see a white puff of cold gas, the torch is actually full, and the issue is likely a clog in the burner head. 4. If nothing happens, the tank is still empty.

Since you are in Ankeny, if you find you're missing the right adapter, the Ace Hardware or the Home Depot on SE Delaware Ave usually carry the Bernzomatic-specific butane canisters that have the correct universal tip built-in.
